{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Fadil Santosa''' is a professor of [[applied mathematics]] and [[statistics]] at [[Johns Hopkins University]], where he is currently the Yu Wu and Chaomei Chen Department Head.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fadil Santosa |url=https://engineering.jhu.edu/faculty/fadil-santosa/ |website=Johns Hopkins Whiting School of Engineering |access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref> Before, he was a professor at the [[University of Minnesota]].

At the University of Minnesota he was director of the  [https://cse.umn.edu/math/minnesota-center-industrial-mathematics Minnesota Center for Industrial Mathematics], and later director of the [[Institute for Mathematics and its Applications]] (IMA) from 2008 to 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=Former Directors |url=https://cse.umn.edu/ima/former-directors |website=Institute for Mathematics and its Applications |publisher=University of Minnesota |access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref>

Santosa is a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi |website=American Mathematical Society |access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref> and the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM).<ref>{{cite web |title=Fellows Directory |url=https://www.siam.org/programs-initiatives/prizes-awards/fellows-program/fellows-directory/ |website=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics |access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref>

Santosa has been recognized with the 2023 SIAM Prize for Distinguished Service to the Profession.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prize History |url=https://www.siam.org/programs-initiatives/prizes-awards/major-prizes-lectures/siam-prize-for-distinguished-service-to-the-profession/prize-history/ |website=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics |access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref> He also received the 2023 Johns Hopkins Diversity Award.<ref>{{cite web |title=2023 Diversity Recognition Awards |url=https://diversity.jhu.edu/assets/uploads/sites/11/2023/05/DLC-Awards-2023-Program-FINAL.pdf |website=Johns Hopkins University |date=2023 |access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref>

Santosa is known for his work in applied mathematics (detailed below) and his efforts to connect academia and industry, which, in addition to the leadership roles mentioned earlier, include co-authoring a guide for mathematicians on finding careers in business, industry, and government.<ref name="bigjobs" />

Santosa holds two patents: for multifocal optical device design and for symbol-based decoding of optical codes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://patents.justia.com/search?q=fadil+santosa |title=Patents search for Fadil Santosa |website=Justia Patents |publisher=Justia |access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref>

==Research==

Santosa's research interests include [[inverse problems]], wave phenomena in complex media, [[photonics|photonic]] devices, and [[optimal design]]. His research includes foundational work on using [[Lp space|L<sup>1</sup>]] [[mathematical optimization|optimization]] to find sparse solutions to inverse problems, with a 1986 paper<ref name="Linear inversion of band-limited re">{{cite journal |last1=Santosa |first1=Fadil |last2=Symes |first2=William W. |title=Linear inversion of band-limited reflection seismograms |journal=SIAM Journal on Scientific and Statistical Computing |volume=7 |issue=4 |pages=1307–1330 |date=1986 |doi=10.1137/0907087}}</ref> now seen as a precursor to methods like compressed sensing and LASSO.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tibshirani |first1=Robert |title=Regression Shrinkage and Selection Via the Lasso |journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B (Methodological) |year=1996 |volume=58 |issue=1 |pages=267–288 |jstor=2346178}}</ref>

Santosa was also one of the first to apply the [[level-set method]] to structural optimization and inverse scattering problems.<ref name="osher2001" />

His PhD advisor was Robert W. Carroll.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fadil Santosa |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=36054 |website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project |publisher=North Dakota State University |access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref>  Santosa was born in Bandung, Indonesia.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fadil Santosa Curriculum Vitae |url=https://engineering.jhu.edu/ams/wp-content/uploads/sites/37/2021/01/CV-Fadil-Santosa-Jan-2021.pdf |website=Johns Hopkins University |access-date=September 20, 2025}}</ref>
